title: Zero-day CP deploy runbook and terraform module notes
content:
Purpose:
This runbook captures an end-to-end, pragmatic deployment and rotation flow for Private Control Plane (VPC/on‑prem) customers. It blends an operator checklist, Terraform module notes, and a minimal upgrade/rollback plan we can follow for initial setup, day-2 scaling, and key rotation windows.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SREs, platform engineers, solutions engineers executing customer installs or upgrades.
- Scope: control plane bootstrap (seed), incremental scaling of CP nodes, KV/cache rotations, and safe terraform-anchored upgrades. Not covering application data plane (edge nodes) in depth — refer to edge runbooks for that.

Assumptions & prerequisites (quick):
- Customer has a VPC with required subnets and NAT/GW, firewall rules approved.
- KMS/HSM credentials and role binding completed.
- Access: operator has cloud admin + ssh bastion access, and the Terraform state backend is configured (remote S3-compatible bucket with locking via DynamoDB or object store + consul lock).
- Minimal image artifact (CP operator container) already pushed to customer registry for air-gapped installs.

Inventory checklist (before you start):
- Terraform state location and lock owner? (terraform.tfstate bucket and lock table)
- K8s cluster control plane endpoint & kubeconfig path
- Backup of etcd/DB snapshot (take fresh snapshot into artifact store)
- Tenant-specific secrets: service accounts, TLS certs, KMS keys
- Gatekeeper: feature flags and operator image digest pinned

Terraform modules: layout and operator notes
- Module layout (high level):
  - modules/network: vpc, subnets, route tables, NATs (idempotent; use existing VPC flows)
  - modules/iam: roles, policies, KMS bindings
  - modules/controlplane: k8s manifests, operator CRDs, node groups, pv provisioning
  - modules/kv: managed redis/consul instances (if used)
  - modules/monitoring: datadog/prom exporters, log forwarders

- Key module knobs to watch:
  - controlplane.replicas (default 3) — lower to 1 only in lab
  - controlplane.node_type (g4dn/p4 equivalent) — use smallest supported for seed ops
  - controlplane.state_backend (s3/consul) — ensure locking enabled
  - iam.operator_assume_role — must be principal with kms:Decrypt for rotation jobs

- Pattern: Keep modules small and composable. Avoid module drift by running `terraform fmt && terraform validate` as pre-commit. PR template must include a `plan` output and state delta notes.

Bootstrapping sequence (zero-day):
1) Preflight check (15-30m): confirm inventory, ensure runner workstation has aws/gcloud creds, kubeconfig access, and that the operator image digest is available.
2) Snapshot DB/etcd (if migrating/upgrading existing CP): create snapshot and store in archive bucket with timestamp.
   - cmd example: etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap-$(date +%Y%m%d).db --endpoints=$ETCD_ENDPOINT --cert=...
3) Apply network and IAM modules first (terraform apply modules/network & modules/iam).
   - verify subnets, route tables, NSGs open for control plane ports.
4) Deploy controlplane module with replicas=1 for initial install, node_type=small, and enable plan-only approval.
   - terraform workspace select <env>; terraform plan -out plan.bin; terraform apply plan.bin
5) Wait for operator pods to reach Ready (kubectl -n redwood get pods). Watch logs: kubectl -n redwood logs -f deployment/redwood-operator
6) Run smoke e2e: create a dummy CP resource and ensure reconciliation completes within 5 minutes.
7) Promote to replicas=3: update controlplane.replicas -> 3 and terraform apply; validate leader election and quorum.
8) Post-installation: collect inventory snapshot: `kubectl get all -n redwood -o wide`, `kubectl get nodes`, `terraform state list` and attach to ticket.

Scaling and rotation (routine scaling event):
- Intent: add N nodes or upgrade node instance class with minimal disruption. Plan window: 30-90m depending on PV reattach times.
- Strategy: rolling scale with cordon/drain and one-at-a-time controlplane pod replacement.
- Steps:
  1) Pre-check cluster health: single region control plane latency < 100ms and all pods Ready.
  2) Bump node_group.desired_count by +1 in Terraform and run plan/apply.
  3) Wait for new node to join and scheduler to accept pods.
  4) Cordon and drain an existing controlplane node: `kubectl cordon <node>`; `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
  5) Confirm pods reschedule and reach Ready. Repeat for subsequent nodes.
  6) After scale completes, run `kubectl get cs`, `kubectl get pods -n redwood` and `terraform state show module.controlplane.aws_autoscaling_group.main` (or equivalent) to verify counts.

Rotation (TLS/KMS/Secret rotation):
- Rotate TLS certs and KMS keys during low traffic windows. High-level flow: generate new certs, stage as secret with suffix `-staged`, point operator to staged secret (feature flag or annotation), let CRDs reconcile, flip traffic, and delete old.
- For KMS keys: new key creation -> grant operator IAM on new key -> run key rotation job -> audit logs. Keep old key enabled for at least 7 days for rollback.

Upgrade plan (operator or controlplane component):
- Goal: Safe, auditable rolling upgrade that is reversible.
- Pre-upgrade: open rollout ticket with plan, create backup snapshot (etcd/db), capture current terraform plan, and tag the current operator image digest in GH.
- Canary path: upgrade one replica (or a single cluster in a fleet) first to validate. Steps:
  1) Create a canary workspace: terraform workspace new canary-<date> or apply with `replicas=1` for test cluster.
  2) Update operator image digest in variables: controlplane.operator_image_digest = sha256:...
  3) terraform plan & apply. Confirm health checks for 30 minutes.
  4) If green, roll rest of cluster with maxUnavailable=1 and pod disruption budget respected.
- Rollback: if significant failure (>=2 critical alerts or >5m unready controlplane), revert to previous operator_image_digest and `terraform apply`. Re-instate DB snapshot only if control plane unable to form quorum.

Terraform state migration considerations:
- When changing backends (S3 -> GCS or similar): ensure state is locked, take a local backup `terraform state pull > state-backup-<date>.json`. Use `terraform init -migrate-state` and validate. Have at least two people present for migration.

Validation & health checks (post-change quick list):
- All controlplane pods Ready and RestartCount < 3 in 1h
- Leader election stable, no split-brain events (operator logs)
- API latency < 200ms 95th percentile for controlplane endpoints
- No database replication lag > 10s
- Alert burn-in: silence non-critical alerts before and re-enable after 30m

Runbook commands and snippets (common):
- Check operator logs: kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=redwood-operator --since=1h
- Drain node safely: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
- Terraform plan & apply: terraform plan -var-file=env.tfvars -out tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
- Snapshot etcd: etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/snap.db --endpoints=${ETCD} --cacert=/etc/etcd/ca.pem --cert=/etc/etcd/client.pem --key=/etc/etcd/client-key.pem

Common failure modes & mitigations:
- Failure: operator crashloop after upgrade -> mitigation: revert image via terraform, scale replicas to 1 to stop churn, gather logs, open SEV if degraded for > 15m.
- Failure: Terraform apply deadlocked due to state lock -> mitigation: identify lock owner and use `aws dynamodb delete-item` only if owner is orphaned (after checking session ttl). Document lock id.
- Failure: New nodes never join -> check CNI config, bootstrap userdata errors, and node IAM role (sts/token).

Checklist for post-change handoff (attach to ticket):
- [ ] Snapshot id and path attached
- [ ] Terraform plan output and apply log attached
- [ ] Pod states (kubectl get pods -n redwood -o wide)
- [ ] Alert statuses and paging contact list updated
- [ ] Rollback steps and known-issue notes in ticket

Escalation & contacts:
- Primary on-call: eng-private-deployments on-call rotation (pagerduty)
- Owners: Aisha Banerjee (owner), Luca Martinez (platform), Priya Nair (infra)
- For legal/security KMS questions: security@redwood.com (ops sec)

Open questions / TODOs (for follow-up):
- Add explicit automated smoke tests post-terraform apply (GH Action) to validate reconciliation.
- Harden module testing with `terraform-compliance` checks in CI for IAM and KMS policies.
- Document a formal rollback play for active migrations with exact etcd restore commands per distro.

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight and link to the canonical operator architecture page for deeper component diagrams. When iterating, update the terraform module knobs section with any new var names introduced by infra.

End of runbook.
